To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new asynchronous pipelined time-to-digital-converter with fine resolution, high throughput, and on-chip digital calibration is presented.
we have developed a 300 MS/s, 1, 76 ps-resolution, 10 b TDC with on-chip digital backgound calibration.
the TDC has a high throughput of 300MS/s, a fine resolution of 1/1.76ps, a good linearity, a low power consumption of 3.6mW and an area of 1.4mm^2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a high-resolution, high-speed, and low-power TDC.
the development and implementation of an asynchronous pipelining time-to-digital conversion technique.
the development of an efficient and robust algorithm for the estimation of parameters in the presence of outliers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TDC presented in this paper has a high throughput, good resolution, and low area and power consumption.
the proposed TDC is suitable for high-speed applications.
the TDC is an important part of many applications and this paper presents a good example of the state of the art.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed the first asynchronous pipeline TDC with digital background calibration and demonstrated its performance in terms of resolution, linearity and throughput.
we have demonstrated a 300-MSps TDC with 1.76-PSR resolution and 10-b ENOB, with a total power consumption of 3.2 mW.
the proposed TDC is the first 10-b asynchronous pipelined time-to-digital conversion architecture with on-chip digital residue subtraction correction and the highest throughput reported to date.
The main takeaway from our work is that
asynchronous clocking can achieve high throughput with low power consumption, and the digital background calibration can improve the linearity of the TDC.
the proposed architecture can achieve a high throughput of 300 MHz, a high resolution of 1 ps, and a good linearity.

asynchronous pipelining is a viable alternative to conventional synchronous pipelining for time-to-digital conversion, and that asynchronous pipelined TDCs are a viable alternative to the more conventional synchronous pipelined TICs for high-resolution, high-speed time measurement.
